frequency_question: How often do submitted Section 123 nuclear cooperation agreements face a successfully passed joint resolution of disapproval that survives or overrides a veto within the statutory window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal 123 agreement transmitted by the executive branch to Congress since the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act of 1978 where a formal review period elapsed. Excludes informal consultations prior to formal submission.

cases.name: Iran Nuclear Agreement review under Corker-Cardin (2015 - JCPOA related framework)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 major named controversial submissions in recent decades; zero instances of successful legislative blocking via joint resolution under the AEA framework.
known_gaps: Older routine 123 agreements (dozens) that passed implicitly without active congressional opposition are excluded as non-controversial baseline background.
skeleton: Formal 123 agreements submitted for congressional review since 1978 times the historical rate of successful blocking joint resolutions.
multiplier: 3 major controversial submissions examined; 0 successful joint resolutions passing both chambers and defeating/bypassing veto.
validity_reason: Statutory mechanisms under the Atomic Energy Act remain stable unless major legislative reform alters the 123 review process.
